sections.h2: Contacting the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
This office keeps the county's land records, along with births, deaths, marriages, military discharges, notary files and maps. Call (252) 641-7924 for counter hours and the street address. Tarboro is the county seat.

When you sell an Edgecombe County house, your signed deed is filed here, usually sent over by the closing attorney. The sections below cover the charges and the local quirks that can slow a recording.

A general document costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that. The excise tax line is $1.00 per $500.00.

The office promises same day processing of filings and requests. If you file by mail, enclose a stamped, self addressed return envelope.

A county resolution requires every deed to carry the Tax Collector's certification before it can be recorded, with one way around it. Instead, the deed can bear a statement that a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that the closing attorney will deliver any delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from the closing proceeds.

An attorney drafting your deed can add that line. If you prepare a deed yourself, stop at the Tax Collector first and ask for the certification.

  • Attorney route: the preparer statement satisfies the resolution, and back taxes come out of your proceeds.
  • Do it yourself route: obtain the certification before bringing the deed to the register.

sections.h2: Can a deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The county's E-Recording page names Simplifile as the vendor and also points to CSC eRecording Solutions. Law firms and title agents with an account can send a deed in without a courier.

A seller with no account should ask the closing attorney to file it. Paper filings follow the state filing standards, which the Real Estate page posts as a PDF beside an Assumed Name form and property check instructions.

sections.h2: What must never appear in a recorded document
sections.html:
Leave out Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver's license, state ID, passport, bank account, credit card and debit card numbers, plus PINs and passwords. G.S. 132-1.10(g)(1) permits such a number only when a law or court order demands it, or when only the last four digits remain.

Filed documents join the official county records, so read yours before signing and ask the preparer to strip anything sensitive.

For Present Use Value purposes, the recording date is the transfer date. A buyer who wants the land to stay in the use value program has 60 days from that date to file a new application.

The new owner also takes on deferred taxes, including those from years before the sale. If the land leaves the program, the current year plus three earlier years become payable with interest. A seller with such land should ask the Tax Assessor about its status before listing or accepting an offer.

  • Farm use needs 10 cultivated acres, and forest use needs 20 forested acres plus a management plan.
  • Farm income must average $1000 a year across the last three years.
  • A sale to an owner who cannot qualify can take the land out of the program.

Each certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate costs $10. Online orders go through Permitium/AIS, which adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees, and the office also takes a mailed application. Birth and death files begin in October 1913, and marriage files begin in 1867.

Heirs selling an inherited house usually need a certified death certificate, so order it early.

sections.h2: How property taxes connect to the deed
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's office bills and collects real estate, personal property and vehicle tax for the county, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns. It also prepares statements of taxes due for attorneys and real estate professionals, and your closing attorney can request one before the sale closes.

Questions about taxes paid or owed go to (252) 641-7810. Questions about a value go to the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855. Our Edgecombe County property tax guide covers rates, listing and appeals.

sections.h2: Rocky Mount and Tarboro homes: which county office?
sections.html:
Recording follows the county where the land lies. A Tarboro house goes to the Edgecombe County office, and so does the Edgecombe side of Rocky Mount. Rocky Mount is divided between Nash and Edgecombe counties and is the largest municipality here, so check which side of the line your parcel sits on before you send the deed.

If one parcel crosses a county line, the excise tax is paid to the register in the county holding the greater share of the value. A parcel in one of the small towns, such as Princeville, Pinetops, Whitakers, Speed, Leggett, Conetoe, Macclesfield or Sharpsburg, still needs its county confirmed.

Ask your closing attorney to confirm the parcel number and the county before the signing appointment. Same day processing only helps when the paper reaches the right office.

1. Get a statement of taxes due from the Tax Collector.
  2. Have the attorney prepare the deed, with the preparer statement or the Tax Collector's certification.
  3. Pay the excise tax with the filing. The seller owes it, and the office collects it with the deed.
  4. Record the deed, ideally electronically through your attorney or title agent.
  5. If a mortgage is being paid off, expect the satisfaction to be recorded at no charge.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the deed, the excise tax and the tax certification still apply.

Edgecombe County had 49,121 residents in the July 2025 estimate, living in 23,604 housing units. About 60.8% of homes are owner occupied, with a median value of $125,100. Recording fees are fixed, so a $125,100 house pays the same page charge as a far costlier one. Only the excise tax follows the price.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage release in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: No. A satisfaction carries no fee, so releasing a mortgage at closing adds no recording charge.

faqs.q: What is the Edgecombe County excise tax rate?
faqs.a: The county prints $1.00 per $500.00. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before recording, and the office collects it along with the deed.

faqs.q: Does Edgecombe County record a deed that lacks a tax certification?
faqs.a: Only if the deed carries the attorney preparer statement. Otherwise the Tax Collector must certify it. The statement must say a North Carolina attorney prepared the deed and the closing attorney will pay delinquent taxes from proceeds.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified birth or death certificate in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: Order online through Permitium/AIS or mail the application for a certified copy. Each copy costs $10, and the online route adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees.

faqs.q: Does the Edgecombe County register accept electronic filing?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts e-recording through Simplifile and also lists CSC eRecording Solutions. Ask your closing attorney or title company to submit the deed.
